title: The lifting lemma of Popescu's theorem
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $\Lambda$ an $R$-algebra and $\pi\in R$ with $\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi)=\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi^2)$ and $\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi)=\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi^2)$ (annihilators of the elements $\pi$, $\pi^2$ in $R$ and of their images in $\Lambda$). Suppose given homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $R/\pi^2R\to\bar C\to\Lambda/\pi^2\Lambda$ with $\bar C$ of finite presentation over $R/\pi^2R$. Then there are an $R$-algebra $D$ and a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $D\to\Lambda$, together with a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $\bar C\to D/\pi D$ such that the diagram formed by $R/\pi^2R\to\bar C\to\Lambda/\pi^2\Lambda$, $R/\pi R\to D/\pi D\to\Lambda/\pi\Lambda$ (the second map induced by $D\to\Lambda$) and the vertical maps $R/\pi^2R\to R/\pi R$, $\bar C\to D/\pi D$, $\Lambda/\pi^2\Lambda\to\Lambda/\pi\Lambda$ commutes, with the following properties: (a) $D$ is of finite presentation over $R$; (b) $R\to D$ is smooth at every prime $\mathfrak q\subset D$ with $\pi\notin\mathfrak q$ (smooth at a prime as in [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]); (c) $R\to D$ is smooth at every prime $\mathfrak q\subset D$ with $\pi\in\mathfrak q$ whose image in $\operatorname{Spec}(D/\pi D)$ lies over (via $\bar C\to D/\pi D$) a prime of $\bar C$ at which $R/\pi^2R\to\bar C$ is smooth; (d) $\bar C/\pi\bar C\to D/\pi D$ is smooth at every prime of $D/\pi D$ lying over a prime of $\bar C$ at which $R/\pi^2R\to\bar C$ is smooth.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07CP (lemma-lifting, line 1421), Section Tag 07CN (section-lifting-lemma), and its proof

proof.text: (Presentation; Noetherianity.) Since $\bar C$ is of finite presentation over $R/\pi^2R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], choose a presentation $\bar C\cong(R/\pi^2R)[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_m)$ and lifts $f_j\in P:=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ of the $\bar f_j$. Put $\bar P=(R/\pi^2R)[x_1,\dots,x_n]=P/\pi^2P$, $I=(f_1,\dots,f_m)\subseteq P$, $\bar I=(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_m)\subseteq\bar P$ its image, and for $E\subseteq\{1,\dots,m\}$, $I_E=(f_j,\ j\in E)$ with image $\bar I_E\subseteq\bar P$. Thus $\bar C=\bar P/\bar I=P/(I+\pi^2P)$; we write $x_i$ also for the images of the variables, and $\bar a$ for the image in $\bar C$ of $a\in P$. $\bar C$ is a finitely generated algebra over the Noetherian ring $R$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], hence Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Let $W\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}\bar C$ be the set of primes at which $R/\pi^2R\to\bar C$ is smooth [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CP (lemma-lifting), lines 1452-1460 ('We choose a presentation ... Since R is Noetherian, so is C-bar'); Stacks writes the presentation over R, we present over R/pi^2R and lift the equations, which is the same up to adding pi^2

proof.text: (Finitely many good elements: Stacks (1), (2).) For each $\bar{\mathfrak q}\in W$ apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-prime-free-conormal-basis] to the ring $R/\pi^2R$, the presentation $\bar C=\bar P/\bar I$ and $\bar{\mathfrak q}$: there are $a_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}\in P$ (lift an element of $\bar P$) with $\bar a_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}\notin\bar{\mathfrak q}$ and $V_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}\subseteq\{1,\dots,m\}$ such that $\bar C_{\bar a}$ is smooth over $R/\pi^2R$, $(\bar I/\bar I^2)_{\bar a}$ is free over $\bar C_{\bar a}$ on the classes of $\bar f_j$, $j\in V_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$, and $\Omega_{\bar C_{\bar a}/(R/\pi^2R)}$ is free of rank $n-|V_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}|$ ($a=a_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$). Let $T\subseteq\bar C$ be the set of all $\bar a_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$. The ideal $(T)$ is finitely generated ($\bar C$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]); each of finitely many generators is a combination of finitely many elements of $T$, so $(T)=(t_1,\dots,t_r)$ with $t_k\in T$. Choose for each $k$ one $\bar{\mathfrak q}$ with $t_k=\bar a_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$ and put $a_k=a_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$, $E_k=V_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$. Then: (1) $W=\bigcup_kD(\bar a_k)$: a prime $\bar{\mathfrak q}\in W$ does not contain $\bar a_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}\in(T)$, so it misses some $t_k$; conversely $\bar C_{\bar a_k}$ smooth gives $D(\bar a_k)\subseteq W$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]; (2) $(\bar I/\bar I^2)_{\bar a_k}$ is free over $\bar C_{\bar a_k}$ on the classes of $\bar f_j$, $j\in E_k$; (2') $\bar C_{\bar a_k}$ is smooth over $R/\pi^2R$ and $\Omega_{\bar C_{\bar a_k}/(R/\pi^2R)}$ is free of rank $n-|E_k|$. Properties (1), (2), (2') only depend on $D(\bar a_k)$ and the ring $\bar C_{\bar a_k}$; so they persist when $a_k$ is replaced by $a'_k\in P$ with $\bar a'_k=\bar a_k^{s}$ for some $s\ge1$ (then $\bar C_{\bar a'_k}=\bar C_{\bar a_k}$).

proof.text: (Nakayama: Stacks (3).) Fix $k$. In $\bar P_{a_k}$ let $J=\bar I\bar P_{a_k}$ and $M=(\bar I/\bar I_{E_k})_{a_k}$, a finitely generated $\bar P_{a_k}$-module. By (2) the localization of $\bar I/\bar I^2$ at $a_k$ is generated by the classes of $\bar f_j$, $j\in E_k$, i.e. $\bar I_{a_k}=(\bar I_{E_k})_{a_k}+(\bar I^2)_{a_k}$ (localization is exact [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]), hence $M=JM$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-one-plus-ideal-annihilator] there is $e\in\bar P_{a_k}$ with $e-1\in J$ and $eM=0$. Write $e-1=\bar b/a_k^N$ with $b\in I$ (lift the numerator from $\bar I$ to $I$), so $e=\overline{(a_k^N+b)}/a_k^N$. Replace $a_k$ by $a'_k=a_k(a_k^N+b)$: since $\bar b=0$ in $\bar C$, $\bar a'_k=\bar a_k^{N+1}$, so (1), (2), (2') persist (Step 2); and $(\bar I/\bar I_{E_k})_{a'_k}$ is a localization of $M$ in which the annihilator $a_k^Ne=\overline{a_k^N+b}$ of $M$ is a unit, so it is $0$. This gives (3): $(\bar I_{E_k})_{a_k}=\bar I_{a_k}$ in $\bar P_{a_k}$. (Stacks says 'replacing $a_k$ by $a_kb_k$'; with $b_k\in I$ that element maps to $0$ in $\bar C$, so the intended replacement is $a_k(a_k^N+b_k)$, as here.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CP (lemma-lifting), lines 1475-1484 ('By (2) and Nakayama's lemma ... After replacing a_k by a_k b_k we get (3)')

proof.text: (Relations (4).) By (3), for every $k$ and $\ell$, $\bar f_\ell/1\in(\bar I_{E_k})_{a_k}$, i.e. $\bar f_\ell/1=\sum_{j\in E_k}(\bar y_j/a_k^s)\bar f_j$ in $\bar P_{a_k}$; equality in $\bar P_{a_k}$ means equality in $\bar P$ after multiplying by a power of $a_k$, so $a_k^t\bar f_\ell=\sum_{j\in E_k}\bar h_j\bar f_j$ in $\bar P$ for some $t$ and $\bar h_j\in\bar P$; lifting to $P$, $a_k^tf_\ell-\sum_{j\in E_k}h_jf_j\in\pi^2P$. Taking one $t$ for all (finitely many) $k,\ell$ and replacing each $a_k$ by $a_k^t$ (allowed by Step 2; (3) persists as $\bar P_{a_k^t}=\bar P_{a_k}$) we obtain $h^j_{k,\ell},g_{k,\ell}\in P$ with (4) $a_kf_\ell=\sum_{j\in E_k}h^j_{k,\ell}f_j+\pi^2g_{k,\ell}$ for all $k\in\{1,\dots,r\}$, $\ell\in\{1,\dots,m\}$; for $\ell\in E_k$ we take instead $h^j_{k,\ell}=a_k\delta_{\ell j}$ and $g_{k,\ell}=0$, for which (4) holds trivially.

proof.text: (The algebra $D$; property (a).) Let $Q=R[x_1,\dots,x_n,z_1,\dots,z_m]$, $p_{k,\ell}=a_kz_\ell-\sum_{j\in E_k}h^j_{k,\ell}z_j-\pi g_{k,\ell}\in Q$ (so $p_{k,\ell}=0$ for $\ell\in E_k$) and $D=Q/(f_j-\pi z_j\ (1\le j\le m),\ p_{k,\ell}\ (1\le k\le r,\,1\le\ell\le m))$ with $R\to D$ the structure map. Finitely many variables and relations: $D$ is of finite presentation over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], which is (a).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CP (lemma-lifting), lines 1495-1506 (definition of D and p_{k,l})

proof.text: (The map $D\to\Lambda$.) Choose $\lambda_i\in\Lambda$ whose class modulo $\pi^2\Lambda$ is the image of $x_i$ under $\bar C\to\Lambda/\pi^2\Lambda$, and for $f\in P$ let $f(\lambda)\in\Lambda$ be its image under the $R$-algebra map $P\to\Lambda$, $x_i\mapsto\lambda_i$. Since $\bar f_j=0$ in $\bar C$, $f_j(\lambda)\in\pi^2\Lambda$: $f_j(\lambda)=\pi^2\mu_j$ with $\mu_j\in\Lambda$. Let $Q\to\Lambda$ be the $R$-algebra map $x_i\mapsto\lambda_i$, $z_j\mapsto\pi\mu_j$. It sends $f_j-\pi z_j$ to $0$, and $p_{k,\ell}$ to $\pi Y$ with $Y=a_k(\lambda)\mu_\ell-\sum_{j\in E_k}h^j_{k,\ell}(\lambda)\mu_j-g_{k,\ell}(\lambda)$; by (4) evaluated at $\lambda$, $\pi^2Y=a_k(\lambda)f_\ell(\lambda)-\sum_jh^j_{k,\ell}(\lambda)f_j(\lambda)-\pi^2g_{k,\ell}(\lambda)=0$, so $Y\in\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi^2)=\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi)$ and $\pi Y=0$. Hence $Q\to\Lambda$ factors through an $R$-algebra map $\psi:D\to\Lambda$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CP (lemma-lifting), lines 1508-1530

proof.text: (The map $\bar C\to D/\pi D$ and the diagram.) The $R$-algebra map $P\to D/\pi D$, $x_i\mapsto x_i$, kills $\pi^2$ and each $f_j=(f_j-\pi z_j)+\pi z_j$, hence factors through $\bar C=P/(I+\pi^2P)$: an $R/\pi^2R$-algebra map $\rho:\bar C\to D/\pi D$. The left square commutes because both composites $R/\pi^2R\to D/\pi D$ are $R$-algebra maps. The right square commutes because $\bar C\to\Lambda/\pi^2\Lambda\to\Lambda/\pi\Lambda$ and $\bar C\xrightarrow{\rho}D/\pi D\xrightarrow{\bar\psi}\Lambda/\pi\Lambda$ are $R$-algebra maps from $\bar C$, which is generated by the $x_i$, both sending $x_i$ to the class of $\lambda_i$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CP (lemma-lifting), lines 1530-1532 ('The map C-bar -> D/pi D is determined by x_i -> x_i (clearly well defined)')

proof.text: (Key equality.) For all $k,\ell$, in $Q$: $\pi p_{k,\ell}=\pi a_kz_\ell-\sum_{j\in E_k}\pi h^j_{k,\ell}z_j-\pi^2g_{k,\ell}=-a_k(f_\ell-\pi z_\ell)+\sum_{j\in E_k}h^j_{k,\ell}(f_j-\pi z_j)$, by substituting $\pi^2g_{k,\ell}=a_kf_\ell-\sum_jh^j_{k,\ell}f_j$ from (4).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CP (lemma-lifting), lines 1534-1546 (the key equality)

proof.text: (Property (b).) Invert $\pi$. By Step 8 every $p_{k,\ell}$ lies in the ideal of $Q_\pi$ generated by the $f_j-\pi z_j=-\pi(z_j-\pi^{-1}f_j)$, so $D_\pi=Q_\pi/(z_j-\pi^{-1}f_j,\ 1\le j\le m)\cong P_\pi=R_\pi[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ as $R$-algebras ($z_j\mapsto\pi^{-1}f_j$). $R\to P$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth], hence $R\to P_\pi$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-principal-localization] [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], so $D_\pi$ is a smooth $R$-algebra. For a prime $\mathfrak q\subset D$ with $\pi\notin\mathfrak q$ the element $g=\pi\notin\mathfrak q$ shows that $R\to D$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]: (b).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CP (lemma-lifting), lines 1547-1551 ('D[1/pi] is isomorphic to R[1/pi][x_1..x_n,z_1..z_m]/(f_j - pi z_j) which is isomorphic to R[1/pi][x_1..x_n] hence smooth over R. This proves (b).')

proof.text:
(The rings $D_k$.) Fix $k$ and let $D_k=Q/(f_j-\pi z_j\ (j\in E_k),\ p_{k,\ell}\ (\ell
otin E_k))$: $n+m$ variables and $|E_k|+(m-|E_k|)=m$ relations (the $p_{k,\ell}$ with $\ell\in E_k$ are $0$). The relations of $D_k$ are among those of $D$, so $D=D_k/J_k$ where $J_k\subseteq D_k$ is the ideal generated by the images of $f_\ell-\pi z_\ell$ ($\ell
otin E_k$) and of $p_{k',\ell}$ ($k'
e k$, all $\ell$), a finitely generated ideal.

proof.text: (The ring $(D_k/\pi D_k)_{a_k}$.) Write $\tilde f$ for the image of $f$ in $(R/\pi R)[x,z]$. By (4) modulo $\pi$, $a_k\tilde f_\ell\in(\tilde f_j,\ j\in E_k)$ for all $\ell$, so in $(R/\pi R)[x]_{a_k}$ the ideals $(\tilde f_j,\ j\in E_k)$ and $(\tilde f_1,\dots,\tilde f_m)$ agree and $(R/\pi R)[x]_{a_k}/(\tilde f_j,\ j\in E_k)=(\bar C/\pi\bar C)_{a_k}$ (as $\bar C/\pi\bar C=(R/\pi R)[x]/(\tilde f_1,\dots,\tilde f_m)$). Hence $(D_k/\pi D_k)_{a_k}=(\bar C/\pi\bar C)_{a_k}[z_1,\dots,z_m]/(a_kz_\ell-\sum_{j\in E_k}h^j_{k,\ell}z_j,\ \ell\notin E_k)\cong(\bar C/\pi\bar C)_{a_k}[z_j,\ j\in E_k]$, solving for $z_\ell=a_k^{-1}\sum_jh^j_{k,\ell}z_j$ ($a_k$ is a unit). This is an isomorphism of $\bar C/\pi\bar C$-algebras for the map $\bar C/\pi\bar C\to(D_k/\pi D_k)_{a_k}$, $x_i\mapsto x_i$, which is well defined by the same computation and is compatible with $\rho$ (Step 7) under $D_k\to D$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CP (lemma-lifting), lines 1559-1570 (computation of (D_k/pi D_k)_{a_k})

proof.text: (Smoothness modulo $\pi$.) By (2'), $(\bar C/\pi\bar C)_{a_k}\cong(R/\pi R)\otimes_{R/\pi^2R}\bar C_{\bar a_k}$ is smooth over $R/\pi R$ [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] (1), with $\Omega_{(\bar C/\pi\bar C)_{a_k}/(R/\pi R)}$ free of rank $n-|E_k|$ [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change]. By Step 11, $(D_k/\pi D_k)_{a_k}$ is a polynomial ring in $|E_k|$ variables over it, hence smooth over it [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth], hence smooth over $R/\pi R$ (composition (2)), and $\Omega_{(D_k/\pi D_k)_{a_k}/(R/\pi R)}$ is free of rank $(n-|E_k|)+|E_k|=n$ [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-polynomial-extension]. Moreover $\bar C/\pi\bar C\to(\bar C/\pi\bar C)_{a_k}$ is smooth (the identity of $\bar C/\pi\bar C$ is smooth, a polynomial ring in $0$ variables, and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-principal-localization]), so $\bar C/\pi\bar C\to(D_k/\pi D_k)_{a_k}$ is smooth (composition), i.e. $\bar C/\pi\bar C\to D_k/\pi D_k$ is smooth at every prime not containing $a_k$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal] [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CP (lemma-lifting), lines 1570-1573 ('In particular (D_k/pi D_k)_{a_k} is smooth over (C-bar/pi C-bar)_{a_k}. By our choice of a_k we have that (C-bar/pi C-bar)_{a_k} is smooth over R/pi R of relative dimension n - |E_k|, see (2).')

proof.text: (The fibre of $R\to D_k$ at $\mathfrak q_k$ is smooth of dimension $n$.) Let $\mathfrak q_k\subset D_k$ be a prime with $\pi\in\mathfrak q_k$ and $a_k\notin\mathfrak q_k$, $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q_k\cap R$ (so $\pi\in\mathfrak p$), $F=D_k\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ the fibre ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $\mathfrak Q_k\subset F$ the kernel of $F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q_k)$. As $\pi\mapsto0$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $F\cong(D_k/\pi D_k)\otimes_{R/\pi R}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $F_{a_k}\cong(D_k/\pi D_k)_{a_k}\otimes_{R/\pi R}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$; by Step 12 it is smooth over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] with $\Omega_{F_{a_k}/\kappa(\mathfrak p)}$ free of rank $n$ [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change]. Since $a_k$ maps to a unit of $\kappa(\mathfrak q_k)$, $a_k\notin\mathfrak Q_k$, so $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to F$ is smooth at $\mathfrak Q_k$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], $F$ is finitely generated over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, and $\Omega_{F/\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\otimes_F\kappa(\mathfrak Q_k)\cong\Omega_{F_{a_k}/\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\otimes\kappa(\mathfrak Q_k)$ [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] has dimension $n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-dimension-differentials] the dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}F$ at $\mathfrak Q_k$ is $n$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CP (lemma-lifting), lines 1573-1576 ('Hence for a prime q_k of D_k containing pi and lying over Spec(C-bar_{a_k}) the fibre ring of R -> D_k is smooth at q_k of dimension n')

proof.text: ($R\to D_k$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q_k$.) For $\mathfrak q_k$ as in Step 13: $D_k$ is $R[n+m\text{ variables}]$ modulo $m$ relations (Step 10) and the fibre has dimension $n=(n+m)-m$ at $\mathfrak Q_k$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-equation-count-fibre-dimension-flat] the local ring map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to(D_k)_{\mathfrak q_k}$ is flat ('syntomic at $\mathfrak q_k$'). $D_k$ is of finite presentation over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to F$ is smooth at $\mathfrak Q_k$ (Step 13), so by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-smooth-fibre-smooth-at-prime] $R\to D_k$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q_k$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CP (lemma-lifting), lines 1576-1581 ('Thus R -> D_k is syntomic at q_k by our count of the number of equations above, see Algebra, Lemma 00ST. Hence R -> D_k is smooth at q_k, see Algebra, Lemma 00TF.')

proof.text: (The relations $f_\ell-\pi z_\ell$ vanish on $D(a_k)$.) In $D_k$ we have $p_{k,\ell}=0$ and $f_j-\pi z_j=0$ for $j\in E_k$, so the key equality (Step 8) gives $a_k(f_\ell-\pi z_\ell)=0$ in $D_k$; as $a_k$ is a unit in $(D_k)_{a_k}$, $f_\ell-\pi z_\ell=0$ in $(D_k)_{a_k}$ for every $\ell$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CP (lemma-lifting), lines 1592-1597

proof.text: (The $p_{k',\ell}$ lie in $\pi(D_k)_{a_k}$.) Let $k',\ell$ be given and $c_j=a_{k'}h^j_{k,\ell}-\sum_{j'\in E_{k'}}h^{j'}_{k',\ell}h^j_{k,j'}\in P$ for $j\in E_k$. In the $\bar C$-module $\bar I/\bar I^2$, (4) gives $a_k\bar f_\ell=\sum_{j\in E_k}h^j_{k,\ell}\bar f_j$ (and likewise for $k'$); computing $a_{k'}a_k\bar f_\ell$ once as $a_{k'}\sum_{j\in E_k}h^j_{k,\ell}\bar f_j$ and once as $a_k\sum_{j'\in E_{k'}}h^{j'}_{k',\ell}\bar f_{j'}=\sum_{j'\in E_{k'}}h^{j'}_{k',\ell}\sum_{j\in E_k}h^j_{k,j'}\bar f_j$ gives $\sum_{j\in E_k}c_j\bar f_j=0$ in $\bar I/\bar I^2$. By (2) every $c_j$ is $0$ in $\bar C_{\bar a_k}$, i.e. $a_k^{N_1}c_j\in I+\pi^2P$; by (3) and finite generation of $\bar I$, $a_k^{N_2}I\subseteq I_{E_k}+\pi^2P$; so $a_k^Nc_j\in I_{E_k}+\pi^2P$ with $N=N_1+N_2$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Expanding the definitions, $a_kp_{k',\ell}-a_{k'}p_{k,\ell}+\sum_{j'\in E_{k'}}h^{j'}_{k',\ell}p_{k,j'}\equiv\sum_{j\in E_k}c_jz_j\pmod{\pi Q}$ (the terms $a_ka_{k'}z_\ell$ and $a_kh^{j'}_{k',\ell}z_{j'}$ cancel). Multiplying by $a_k^N$: $a_k^{N+1}p_{k',\ell}$ lies in the ideal of $Q$ generated by $I_{E_k}$, $\pi$ and the $p_{k,\cdot}$. In $(D_k)_{a_k}$ the $p_{k,\cdot}$ vanish and $f_j=\pi z_j$ for $j\in E_k$, so $I_{E_k}\subseteq\pi(D_k)_{a_k}$; as $a_k$ is a unit, $p_{k',\ell}\in\pi(D_k)_{a_k}$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CP (lemma-lifting), lines 1597-1630 (the Einstein-summation computation; Stacks' '(I-bar_k/I-bar_k^2)_{a_k} is free' is (2) for I-bar/I-bar^2)

proof.text: (The kernel $J_k$ vanishes at $\mathfrak q_k$.) Let $\mathfrak q_k$ be as in Step 13. By the key equality for $k'$, $\pi p_{k',\ell}=-a_{k'}(f_\ell-\pi z_\ell)+\sum_{j'\in E_{k'}}h^{j'}_{k',\ell}(f_{j'}-\pi z_{j'})$, which is $0$ in $(D_k)_{a_k}$ by Step 15. With Step 16, $p_{k',\ell}=\pi y$ with $y\in(D_k)_{a_k}$ and $\pi^2y=0$. Pass to $(D_k)_{\mathfrak q_k}$, a localization of $(D_k)_{a_k}$. By Step 14 there is $g\notin\mathfrak q_k$ with $(D_k)_g$ smooth over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], hence flat [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat]; $(D_k)_{\mathfrak q_k}$ is a localization of $(D_k)_g$, flat over it [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], hence flat over $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp] [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. By [lem-weil-pbc-annihilator-element-flat-base-change], $\mathrm{Ann}_{(D_k)_{\mathfrak q_k}}(\pi^i)=\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi^i)(D_k)_{\mathfrak q_k}$ for $i=1,2$, and these agree since $\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi)=\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi^2)$. So $\pi y=0$, i.e. $p_{k',\ell}\mapsto0$ in $(D_k)_{\mathfrak q_k}$. Together with Step 15 all generators of $J_k$ (Step 10) vanish in $(D_k)_{\mathfrak q_k}$: $(J_k)_{\mathfrak q_k}=0$.

split_report.summary: Statement checked against Stacks 07CP and kept; stmt_deps gain def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra. Proof written in 18 steps following the Stacks proof line by line: presentation and Noetherianity, choice of a_1..a_r via Lemma 07C6 (new node lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-prime-free-conormal-basis, which also records the freeness of Omega used for 'relative dimension n - |E_k|'), Nakayama (3), relations (4), D and D -> Lambda (Ann_Lambda condition), C-bar -> D/pi D and the diagram, the key equality, (b) via D[1/pi] = R[1/pi][x], the rings D_k, (D_k/pi)_{a_k} as polynomial ring, smoothness mod pi with Omega of rank n (new node lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-polynomial-extension), fibre dimension n (new node for Algebra 00TT (1)=>(3)), syntomic by equation count (new node for 00ST(3)+00SW) and smooth by 00TF (new node), then the comparison D_k -> D at q via the annihilator condition (lem-weil-pbc-annihilator-element-flat-base-change) and a principal localization, giving (c) and (d). Deviations: Topology 0052 (quasi-compactness of the smooth locus) replaced by the finite generation of an ideal of the Noetherian ring C-bar; Stacks' 'replace a_k by a_k b_k' corrected to a_k(a_k^N + b_k); the local-ring isomorphism D_q = (D_k)_{q_k} is turned into an isomorphism of principal localizations. The citer lem-weil-pbc-popescu-reduce-to-field uses (a), (b), (c) and the diagram; (d) is proved as in Stacks.
